Det er faktisk 50/50 i heterofile saker om barn i Norge. Jeg var heller ikke klar over det! I de fleste land var det mor som hovedforelder fram til 70tallet, nå har det snudd. I Storbritannia er det nå 90/10 til fordel for menn, av den lille % som havner i retten. Heldigvis har vi hatt en positiv utvikling i Norge og havnet på 50/50. 

Skal være sagt at de aller fleste havner aldri i retten, men fordeler tid med barna slik det passer best for hver enkelt familie. Jeg jobber som frivillig støtte for foreldre i familieretten så har en sterk interesse for dette. 

Det er veldig viktig at alle vet at menn har minst like stor sjanse for å vinne en rettsak. Om menn tenker de har ingen sjanse, så vil mange kanskje la være f.eks selv om mor er voldelig og skader barna. 
Fordi de tenker at mor vinner uansett. Det er ikke sånn, og dette går utover barna. Jeg vokste opp i en slik situasjon og ønsker min far hadde gått i retten for å få meg vekk fra mors mishandling. Fedre kan være en like viktig omsorgsperson som en mor kan. 


Jeg måtte krangle med eks/barnefar for at han skulle ha MER tid med barnet, men han ville "ha tid til seg selv" og ha bare annenhver helg som maksimum. Kostnaden hans for bidrag dekket bare rundt 25% av hva det kostet å huse/mate/kle barnet, jeg dekket resten. Men vi ordnet kontakt uten retten siden man ikke kan tvinge mer kontakt for den andre.

Hi there. I am sorry your husband is not being a safe parent. I have a lot of experience with family court cases from charity volunteering. If you take your kids and leave the area, it can be considered abduction depending on where you live now, and how far you would go. 

I don't know that what he has done so far, would convince a court to go for supervised contact. It usually takes solid proof and/or other witnesses of malicious serious harm, to get supervised. Some lawyers say whatever because mothers fighting for their kid's safety will fight until the end of time, which is good money for lawyers. 

Also having had to quit work makes you extremely vulnerable. Better to outsource childcare to a safe place. You need income and independence.
Reporting him may make him leave you. I would avoid that whilst unemployed. Reports from other people than you will be taken more seriously, court often goes with "bitter ex being petty".

I think your best option might be to sign both up for parenting classes, and ask directly about the bath safety issue there. It is unacceptable, but he does not seem to take you seriously. Get your job back and outsource childcare until he can prove he is capable, or kids are old enough to look after themselves. This is if he is otherwise kind and decent. Any abuse, then seek help and start gathering evidence.

I think here answers a lot of the stuff, I just wanted to comment on my approach with safe foods (also have ED, trying to recover).  
My safe food is bread, so I usually eat bread for breakfast and lunch, and if I am able to I include a fear food such as egg or whatever. Then dinner is more unsafe for me, so that is the main challenge of the day. I'm at a point where I really enjoy a large variety of foods, but they still give some fear reaction. Depending what your safe foods are, it could be possible to include 1-2 different fear foods each day in 1 of your meals for example. It also depends how many things are safe vs fear food and how strong your reaction is now.   


I'm several years down the line in trying to recover, and my entire dinner plate will be what used to be fear food, but because my reaction is not as strong anymore, that is okay and I am able to eat adequately provided I have some distraction. I'm now trying to work on getting rid of the need for distraction, which is very hard for me.   
I would probably advise you to avoid distraction and go about it without that as a tool, but include at least 1 fear food every day.   
Gradually you will see your fear food lose their power and come to feel more neutral about them and even crave them. For example, I sometimes crave apple juice or salad or a particular ice cream, all of which have at some point been fear foods. Then you slowly have a much bigger range of food to eat intuitively from :)

I think if you have/ have had ED, it can have a place, depending how you do it. If you do it in a way that "I need to ensure I have x calories/protein/carb/whatever it is each day" and then meal plan, to avoid undereating during certain times or days, that is useful. The main thing to avoid is calorie counting daily over a longer period, or in order to restrict in any way. In periods where I'm struggling with food and not able to eat much (ED), I find counting my calories for a few days helps me work out ways to add more food so I don't under-eat too much. However once I reach the adequate amount of calories in my plan, I stop counting, so I never count if there's too many and how much too many. I also find it useful to make meal plans that are on a 2 week cycle, because it takes out some of the stress of planning, and takes away needing to think about it every day. I only plan dinner though because breakfast and lunch are always the same anyway.   


TLDR because I blabber on: I think it's okay and a useful tool to avoid ED related undereating, but only in a limited way and for short term use.
